title: The Very Scientific Snack Test
coreQuestion: How does Jacey decide whether food is safe, interesting, or worth investigating?

food_01_opening.dialogue: Question! If a snack looks suspicious, smells suspicious, and was left unlabeled in a science-adjacent place… is it food, evidence, or a trap?

choices.label: Please do not eat the mystery snack.
It depends. Did Kouji touch it first?

food_01_safety.dialogue: Oh. Right. Food is supposed to have provenance. And ingredients. And not be next to jars with handwriting that says things like ‘do not inhale’.

choices.label: Jace, have you eaten unlabeled things before?

food_01_science_adjacent.dialogue: It means it was on a table near beakers, notebooks, three spoons, and one very judgmental sticky note. Which is basically a crime scene with better lighting :D

choices.label: That is not how kitchens work.
What did the sticky note say?

food_01_kouji.dialogue: That is a very useful diagnostic question! If Kouji touched it first, it is either safe, stolen, cursed, part of an escape route, or all four. So we need a control group.

choices.label: You are not making a control group.
What would your food test even measure?

food_01_pause.dialogue: Sometimes I think food is just chemistry wearing a friendlier outfit. Which is nice! But also suspicious.

food_01_label_rule.dialogue: Okay! New rule: if the food has no label, I ask first. If the label has more than three warning symbols, I ask twice. If the label is missing because someone removed it, then it becomes a mystery and I am allowed to investigate but not chew. Probably.

food_01_crystalized_tea.dialogue: Not recently! There was one time I wondered if crystallized compounds dissolved faster in hot water, but apparently the important part was not the dissolving. The important part was that some leaves are ‘medically alarming’ and ‘not tea’ and ‘Jace, why are you like this.’

food_01_kitchen_rules.dialogue: Then kitchens should stop containing knives, heat, chemicals, timers, unlabeled leftovers, and people saying ‘just eyeball it.’ That is not a room. That is a trial waiting to happen.

food_01_sticky_note.dialogue: It said, ‘Do not eat.’ But it did not say what not to eat. The snack? The note? The table? The concept of temptation? This is why precise wording matters!

food_01_no_control_group.dialogue: Okay. No control group. I can do that. It is probably good when people stop me before the experiment becomes a hospital story. I do not always know which part is dangerous until someone points at it.

food_01_food_test.dialogue: The test measures five things! One: smell. Two: texture. Three: whether it makes someone else yell before I touch it. Four: emotional aura. Five: if it has raisins pretending to be chocolate chips, because that is legally deception.

achievement.title: THE VERY SCIENTIFIC SNACK TEST // COMPLETE
